summary: The habits every enterprise seller needs before any framework: research, questions, listening, control of the call.

skills.label: Account research
skills.definition: Arrive with a point of view on the account before the first question.
skills.evidence: The buyer confirms or corrects your account hypothesis.

talk_track.move: Open with what you already know, then ask why.
talk_track.strong: I saw fraud operations moved under the CIO last quarter. What prompted that?
talk_track.weak: Can you tell me a bit about your company?
talk_track.proof: Buyer confirms or corrects your hypothesis about the account

rep.buyer_line: Before we start, what do you already know about how we run things here?
rep.off_move: I have not looked into it yet. Could you walk me through the basics?

skills.label: Discovery questioning
skills.definition: Ask open, layered questions that uncover how work happens today.
skills.evidence: The buyer describes their current process in their own steps.

talk_track.move: Ask how the work runs today, step by step, before you suggest anything.
talk_track.strong: Walk me through how an alert gets worked today, from flag to close.
talk_track.weak: Would faster alert triage help you?
talk_track.proof: Buyer describes the current process in their own steps

rep.buyer_line: We are open to ideas. Where do you want to start?
rep.off_move: Let me show you a quick demo of what we can do.

skills.label: Listening and summarizing
skills.definition: Play the buyer’s words back so they know you heard the real problem.
skills.evidence: The buyer confirms your summary, or corrects it.

talk_track.move: Summarize in their words and check you got it right.
talk_track.strong: So the real cost is analyst hours, not missed fraud. Did I get that right?
talk_track.weak: Great, that makes sense. Moving on.
talk_track.proof: Buyer confirms your summary of their problem

rep.buyer_line: Honestly the bigger issue is the hours my team burns, not the misses.
rep.off_move: Got it. Our product handles misses really well, so let me explain that.

skills.label: Up-front contract
skills.definition: Agree the agenda, the time and the possible outcomes at the start.
skills.evidence: The buyer agrees to the agenda and how the call will end.

talk_track.move: Set time, agenda and outcome, and give the buyer permission to say no.
talk_track.strong: We have 20 minutes. If this is useful we agree a next step. If not, we say so. Fair?
talk_track.weak: Thanks for the time. Let me tell you about our company.
talk_track.proof: Buyer agrees to the agenda and outcome

rep.buyer_line: Thanks for making time. We have about twenty minutes.
rep.off_move: Great, I have a 30-slide deck, so I will move quickly.

skills.label: Objection handling
skills.definition: Understand an objection before you answer it: acknowledge, clarify, respond, confirm.
skills.evidence: The buyer narrows the objection to one root cause you can address.

talk_track.move: Acknowledge, then ask a clarifying question before you answer.
talk_track.strong: That is a fair concern. When you say liability, is it the decision itself or the audit trail?
talk_track.weak: Do not worry, our model is very accurate.
talk_track.proof: Buyer narrows the objection to one root cause

rep.buyer_line: If the model gets a decision wrong, who carries the liability, you or us?
rep.off_move: Our accuracy is industry leading, so that will not happen.

skills.label: Next-step control
skills.definition: End every conversation with a dated next step and a named owner.
skills.evidence: The buyer commits to a named owner and a date.

talk_track.move: Propose a specific next step with a date, owner and purpose.
talk_track.strong: Can we put 30 minutes with your CISO on the calendar for Tuesday?
talk_track.weak: I will send some information over.
talk_track.proof: Buyer agrees a named owner and a date

rep.buyer_line: This was useful. What happens next?
rep.off_move: I will follow up by email sometime next week.
